title: Seller Microfold: Platform Differentiator Flipbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose: tiny, high-impact flipbook for SEs and sellers to run a 3-minute investor-style differentiation demo and a 5-minute follow-up on SLOs/costs. Focus: fast memory, microfacts, two canonical customer stories, one graph, one fallback script.

Notes to self (voice of SE): keep it crisp; buyer wants latency, cost predictability, and reliable fallbacks. Use numbers where possible. Avoid deep model architecture talk unless asked.

Slide 1 — Title & Hook (30s)
- Title: Redwood Inference: predictable inference, on your terms
- Speaker note: open with one line: "We turn variable LLM cost/perf into a predictable engineering contract — across hosted, reserved, and private."
- Talking bullets: 1-sentence mission, 2-sentence value prop for platform engineers.

Slide 2 — One-liner comparison (20s)
- Quick frame: "What we solve vs. other LLM clouds" (table-free: three columns: problem, other clouds, Redwood).
- Key line to memorize: "We trade raw model access for operational economics: latency SLOs, predictable unit cost, and a standard API across environments."

Slide 3 — Two canonical use cases (30s)
- Use case A: High-throughput chat widget (customer-facing search + RAG). Needs: 99th pct latency < 300ms for 95% of prod calls, burst capacity, and predictable token spend.
- Use case B: Regulated private deployment (on-prem or VPC) with audit logs and KMS. Needs: private control plane, HSM/KMS integration, long-tail sequence support.
- Speaker note: name-drop typical customers: fintech fraud ops, healthcare summarization.

Slide 4 — Quick economics (60s)
- Sample micro-econ vignette for chat widget (numbers are placeholders to edit with actual pricebook):
  - Baseline: open model on general cloud (unoptimized): median latency 220ms, per-token infra cost $0.004; unpredictable 95th latency spikes to 1.1s under load.
  - Redwood optimized stack: median latency 170ms, 95th percentile 310ms, effective per-token infra cost $0.0026 via batching + KV caching.
- Seller script: "If you care about latency tail and steady TCO, we can typically reduce per-token infra costs by ~30% while tightening the tail — helps ops and finance."
- Slide CTA: "Ask: what are your current median and 95p latencies and tokens/month?"

Slide 5 — Fallback story + scripting (90s)
- Why fallbacks matter: keeps product available when preferred variant is saturated or in maintenance.
- Example flow (microplay):
  1) Primary: high-quality open model (q8 quant) in region-a
  2) Canary fallback: lighter quantized variant (q4/INT8) — preserves 95% of answer quality for prompt types A/B
  3) Policy: route <10ms added latency to fallback, monitor hallucination rate in eval set X
- SE script (to read): "If you expect steady throughput bursts, we'll set a two-tier fallback so your UX stays within latency SLOs while cost caps remain intact. We can demo a simulated 30% traffic spike and show graceful degradation live."
- Quick checklist for demo: model pair, quantization profile, sequence length distribution, fallback thresh (error/timems).

Slide 6 — Observable signals & the handoff (40s)
- What we show in Console: token-level cost by route, latency heatmap by model and sequence length, rollout traces for canary/A-B, alert tied to prompt eval regression.
- Handoff script for SE->PO: "Here's the SLO we recommend; if you want to tighten tail we'll reserve Dedicated capacity and configure autoscale bursts" (link to SLO simulator).

Slide 7 — Rapid pilot blueprint (60s)
- 3-step pilot (timeboxed):
  1) 7-day integration: SDK + 2 sample endpoints, perf baseline collection.
  2) 14-day tuning: batch & cache rules, fallback policy, monitor.
  3) 30-day measurement: cost delta, latency tail, and sampled quality regressions.
- Seller line: "Pilot commitment: low friction, analytics you can own — if you like results, we scale to dedicated pools."

Slide 8 — Objection riffs (quick cards, 10–20s each)
- "We have our own infra": "Great — Redwood layers on top, same API, or we do a private deployment with your networking controls."
- "Concerned about quality drift": "We tie regressions to prompt sets and automatically notify with sample outputs; we recommend a 1-week eval cadence."
- "Pricing surprises": "Token-level analytics and per-route quotas; we can gate spend with pre-configured budget hooks."

Slide 9 — Two quick demos to prep (notes for SE)
- Demo A: Latency tail drill (show heatmap, flip to canary, re-run synthetic spike).
- Demo B: Cost change after enabling KV prefix cache + batching (run before/after token counts and cost breakdown).
- Pre-demo checklist: demo user project id, sample prompt set (5 queries), synthetic traffic runner, link to canary config.

Slide 10 — Leave-behind (30s)
- One-pager link + pilot checklist + next steps: schedule pilot kickoff, request initial traffic numbers, access to sample prompt sets.
- Draft email snippet for follow-up included below (copy/paste):
  "Thanks for your time today. As discussed, attached is the 3-step pilot plan and the small set of prompts we used for the latency drill. If you can share median/95p latencies and tokens/month, we’ll prepare a tightened proposal for Dedicated capacity. — Sofia"

Appendix — Quick cheat sheet for SEs (editable bullets)
- Memorize: median vs 95p latencies, per-token cost delta, fallback policy template name.
- Quick urls: confluence pilot template (confluence:GM-pilot-template), JIRA pilot ticket template (JIRA:GM-3421).
- Open questions to capture during discovery: peak qps, acceptable degradation modes, compliance needs (KMS/HSM, egress constraints).

Draft status & next steps:
- Needs: 1) real pricebook figures from product ops, 2) final screenshots from Console metrics team, 3) two vetted demo projects from Solutions Eng.
- Action owners: Marcus to wire demo projects (due 2024-11-09), Riya to pull Console screenshots (due 2024-11-06), Liam to sanity-check scripts (due 2024-11-04).

Rough notes: this is intentionally compact — think of it as a pocket flipbook for SEs to carry through short discovery calls. Keep versions under 2 slides per outcome.
